name: The Fifth Avenue Hotel
positioning: Independent hotel in Manhattan's NoMad that pairs a restored 1907 landmark mansion with a modern glass tower, designed by Martin Brudnizki
best_for: Travelers who want a design- and art-filled base in NoMad
Guests who value butler service and in-room touches

facts.text: The hotel is at 1 West 28th Street, at the corner of Fifth Avenue and West 28th Street in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood.
The hotel is within walking distance of Madison Square Park, the Flatiron Building, the Empire State Building, Fifth Avenue shopping, Eataly and Koreatown.
The hotel is built on the former estate of Mrs. Charlotte Goodridge, a Gilded Age hostess.
The mansion housed a fine art gallery before architects McKim, Mead & White reimagined it as the Second National Bank.
The restored 1907 landmark mansion stands beside a contemporary glass tower.
Pae White's Bugs & Drugs tapestry hangs in the lobby.
Photographs by William Klein, Gordon Parks and Melvin Sokolsky hang on the walls.
All rooms have marble bathrooms, stocked maxibars, Nespresso coffee makers and a personal tablet to manage the room.
Each room has complimentary soft drinks and snacks, high-speed Wi-Fi and a personal tablet.
Guests have access to the hotel's luxury house car.
The Portrait Bar is named for the collection of artwork on its wood-paneled walls.

highlights.text: After a 10-year restoration by Flâneur Hospitality, the original brick and limestone Renaissance-style palazzo is joined by a 24-story modern glass tower.
Designer Martin Brudnizki brought both the mansion and the tower to life in rich palettes and worldly curiosities.
The flâneur suite has a terrace with a Japanese garden and a soaking tub overlooking the New York skyline.
Signature Suites have a garden terrace with a view of Manhattan.
Guests can order a martini ritual to their room, where a martini butler stirs or shakes the drink.

considerations.text: Public spaces are in the historic mansion, while most rooms and suites are in the modern glass tower.
Café Carmellini welcomes both hotel guests and visitors, and reservations are recommended.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing typical of a Fifth Avenue location.
